text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The presidents of the three Baltic states signed in Riga a joint declaration and discussed trilateral cooperation between Latvia, Estonia and Lithuania. They also adopted a joint statement urging their inclusion into NATO.
- President Ulmanis announced at a press conference that it was not so essential to mention the 1920 peace treaty with Russia when discussing the issue of the Russian-Latvian border.

- Russian President Boris Yeltsin has appointed Alexander Udaltsov as Russia's new ambassador to Latvia. He has served as the deputy head of the second European department of the Russian foreign ministry.
- Four policeman from Riga Municipal police rapid reaction force were sentenced to prison on charges of extortion, abuse of power and taking hostages.
- The leading party Latvia's way is likely at its congress this Saturday to re-elect Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs as party chairman.
- An Uzbek parliamentary delegation arrived on a three-day visit.
- The cabinet considered more than 500 proposals to amend next year's budget draft and most of them were rejected.

- The cabinet approved and sent to parliament draft amendments to the law on custom tariffs. They envisage that timber export duties will be reduced by 50 percent from January 1997 and abolished from January 1999.
- A conference on international tourism in Latvia opened in Riga with more than 220 participants.

- The volume of credits issued by Latvian banks dropped from 500 million lats at the start of 1995 to 250 million lats at the start of this year and have stagnated at this level ever since. Meanwhile, the assets of commercial banks climbed to 961 million lats and deposits have recovered to 670 million lats from 487 million lats just after the crisis.

- The ferry Rus today starts operating the ferry line between Riga and Stockholm. It will leave Riga for Stockholm three times a week. The boat is being leased by a Swedish company from the Russian Far East shipping company.
